cards.definitions: The network is a finite connected undirected simple graph G=(V,E), n=|V|. Nodes have distinct O(log n)-bit identifiers, communication ports and a common polynomial upper bound on n. They communicate synchronously, with O(log n) bits per edge in each direction per round, and unrestricted local computation. No graph decomposition is supplied. A first-order formula uses vertex variables, equality, adjacency, Boolean operations and vertex quantifiers. Here φ has one free variable x. It is local if some fixed radius r makes its truth at v depend only on the rooted induced neighborhood of all vertices at graph distance at most r from v. The formula and r are fixed independently of n. A graph class has bounded expansion if for every integer s≥0 there is a constant b_s bounding the average degree of every s-shallow minor of every graph in the class. Such a minor is formed by contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of radius at most s, with optional vertex/edge deletions and with parallel edges and loops suppressed. The constructive source assumes a computable bound as a function of s; the class and its bound are fixed, not arbitrary input. The required output at each node v is a Boolean bit equal to the truth value of φ(v). The hidden round constant may depend on φ and C, but not on n, the graph or the identifiers.
cards.answer_criterion: The affirmative result is Theorem 1.4, formally Theorem 4.1, of the full version published at STOC 2026. It gives exactly the required deterministic simultaneous marking algorithm, and additionally permits a fixed finite set of unary vertex labels.

cards.definitions: A simple undirected graph has vertex set [n]={1,…,n} and an edge set E_n of unordered pairs of distinct vertices. For a permutation π of [n], π(E_n)={{π(u),π(v)}:{u,v}∈E_n}. The symmetric difference A△B consists of elements belonging to exactly one of A,B, so the robustness inequality counts changed unordered edges. A graph is self-ordered if its only automorphism is the identity; positive robustness implies this. Given a graph H=([n],F) isomorphic to G_n, there is therefore a unique bijection φ:[n]→[n] satisfying {u,v}∈F iff {φ(u),φ(v)}∈E_n. The local algorithm receives n and a vertex v of H in binary, can query whether any pair is adjacent in H, and must output φ(v). Correctness is required for each H and each v separately, with probability over its internal coins. It is promised an exact isomorphic copy, not a graph with adversarial edge corruptions. Queries are adaptive and each answer is one bit; the polylogarithmic running time counts ordinary computation as well as oracle calls. The family’s canonical adjacency algorithm receives (n,u,v) in binary and decides {u,v}∈E_n. Uniform means fixed algorithms across the family, with no n-dependent advice; poly(log n) means C(log₂(n+1))^a for constants C,a independent of n,H,v. The statement concerns the asymptotic infinite family asserted by the construction; finitely many small sizes do not affect its guarantees. The oracle is the adjacency predicate of a dense graph, not an oracle listing a selected neighbor.
cards.answer_criterion: The affirmative resolution must simultaneously supply the robust graph family, its efficient construction and a polylogarithmic-time local self-ordering algorithm under arbitrary relabelling. cards.definitions: A finite relational vocabulary τ consists of finitely many relation symbols of specified finite arities and finitely many constant symbols, with no positive-arity function symbols. A finite τ-structure A has a finite nonempty domain, interprets each r-ary relation as a subset of A^r, and interprets each constant as an element of A. Equality has its usual meaning. First-order formulas use these atomic predicates and equality, Boolean connectives, and quantifiers ∃x,∀x over the domain; a sentence has no free variables. A formula is in prenex form if a sequence of quantifiers precedes a quantifier-free matrix. Σ_j contains sentences with at most j consecutive blocks of like quantifiers, starting existentially; Π_j is the corresponding universal-starting class. Lower fragments and quantifier-free sentences are included using vacuous padding, valid for nonempty domains. Block lengths are arbitrary finite numbers; k bounds the number of blocks, not the total number of quantifiers. A⊆B means A’s domain is a subset of B’s, every constant has the same interpretation, and each relation of A is exactly the restriction of B’s relation to tuples in A. Thus an extension may add vertices and relations involving new vertices, but cannot change atomic facts on old vertices. The finite models of φ are extension-closed if A⊆B and A⊨φ imply B⊨φ for all finite τ-structures A,B. Equivalence in the finite means A⊨φ iff A⊨ψ for every finite τ-structure A; no equivalence on infinite structures is required. The vocabulary stays fixed when replacing φ by ψ, so no new predicates, constants or built-in order may be added. The question asserts existence of an equivalent sentence, not a uniform translation-time or sentence-length bound.
cards.answer_criterion: Settle the Π_k-collapse assertion and its stronger Σ_{k−1}-collapse version under the stated quantifiers. A positive answer requires a same-vocabulary equivalent sentence for every eligible φ. Refutation of either assertion requires an even k≥4 and a finite vocabulary and extension-closed Σ_k sentence having no equivalent sentence in that target fragment over finite structures. A separation at odd k or one that changes the vocabulary does not settle these assertions.
